name: Croatia: participant-facing document QC
item_format: Each result records the item id, the outcome, a short rationale and evidence (quoted passage and source locator) or an explicit gap.

items.check: Trial title, EU trial number where available, sponsor, investigational medicines, comparator, indication, phase and participant group match the final application.
Purpose and reason for invitation are understandable and do not promise benefit.
Global and Croatian target enrolment figures are stated and match the approved planning data.
Randomisation, blinding, placebo, rescue treatment and treatment assignment are explained as in the protocol.
items.applies_when: protocol uses randomisation, blinding, placebo or rescue treatment

items.check: Trial duration, treatment duration, follow-up, visit frequency, inpatient stays, remote contacts and end-of-trial arrangements match the protocol.
Foreseeable risks, unknown risks, expected benefits, lack of expected direct benefit and alternative treatments match the latest investigator's brochure and protocol.
Emergency contacts and medical advice are appropriate for Croatia and the participating site.
Every procedure matches the schedule of activities: screening, washout, dosing, blood draws, imaging, biopsies, questionnaires, devices, diaries, recordings, home visits and long-term follow-up.
Blood and tissue volumes, sample frequency, fasting, contraception, pregnancy testing and prohibited medicines match the protocol.
Optional activities are identified as optional; optional sample donation, genetics, future research or recordings do not appear required for main-trial participation.
Foreseeable burdens (travel, waiting time, overnight stays, device use, dietary limits, return of unused medicine) are explained.
Withdrawal language distinguishes stopping trial treatment, withdrawing from follow-up, withdrawing an optional consent and requesting action on stored samples where applicable.
Planned home delivery, home nursing, transport, payment provider, recording, wearable or digital platform appears in both the participant document and the application.
items.applies_when: logistics.imp_home_delivery or data.other_third_party or any digital or vendor element

items.check: The main decision to join the trial has clear signature and date fields.
Every optional choice offers both DA and NE, and neither answer affects main-trial participation unless scientifically necessary and stated in the protocol.
The participant (or representative) and the physician or dentist conducting the consent interview sign and date the document when consent is obtained.
No participant signature is requested at CTIS submission; the submitted version is blank.
Consent occurs before any trial-specific procedure and the participant receives a signed copy.
Routine electronic consent is not proposed; only narrow exceptional electronic consent followed by in-person paper consent.
Inability to write uses an impartial witness and is not confused with inability to understand or decide.
Refusal, dissent and later withdrawal are respected without adverse consequences.

sections.title: Population and document coverage
sections.instruction: Map every inclusion pathway in the protocol to an informed consent set (see requirements.json population_sets).

items.check: Every inclusion pathway in the protocol maps to a population, and every population has its full document set from population_sets (main, representative, assent bands, re-consent and other documents that apply).
The main competent-adult informed consent is one unified information and signature document.
Healthy volunteers: absence of therapeutic intent, practical restrictions, confinement where applicable, payment and reproductive precautions explained.
Minors: every recruited age band has the correct assent statement, and parent or guardian consent is provided.
Adults lacking capacity: understandable participant information and a legal-representative document.
Article 35 emergency enrolment: approved initial process and later participant or representative consent provided.
Participant who cannot write: impartial-witness pathway and attestation added.
Pregnancy follow-up: separate documents for a pregnant participant and a participant's pregnant partner, with minor and representative versions where relevant.
Optional genetics, biobanking or future use: a separate consent where Croatian guidance requires it.
items.applies_when: research.optional_substudy or samples.future_use_outside_protocol or data.future_use_outside_protocol or samples.genetic_analysis_optional

items.check: Separate consent for a required caregiver or study partner, a named contact person whose personal details are collected, and home delivery of investigational medicine.
The data controller and relevant representatives are identified with usable contact details.
Processing purposes, categories of personal and health data, recipients, coded identifiers, access, retention, transfers, safeguards and participant rights are stated.
Informed consent to trial participation is not equated with consent as the legal basis for every personal-data processing operation.
Which data may continue to be used after withdrawal, and why, is explained without suggesting that the participant has no data-protection rights.
The sponsor or controller privacy contact and the Croatian Personal Data Protection Agency (AZOP) complaint route are included.
No blanket clause allows the sponsor or investigator to contact outside healthcare professionals for health information; health information is obtained from the participant or legal representative.
If the participant is encouraged to inform a family physician, the participant chooses and performs that communication, and a physician letter is offered.
Each home-delivery, home-nursing, transport, reimbursement, technology or other vendor receiving identifiable participant data is identified with its role.
An emergency contact, caregiver, partner or other third party who provides personal data has a separate notice and consent process where required.
items.applies_when: consent.emergency_contact_collected or consent.caregiver_required or pregnancy.partner_follow_up or data.other_third_party

items.check: What samples are collected, why, by whom, where processed, where stored, for how long and what happens at the end of the trial is stated.
Protocol-required analysis is distinguished from optional substudies, repository donation, future research, genetic testing and whole-genome or whole-exome sequencing.
Coded versus anonymised is explained accurately; anonymisation is not claimed if a re-identification key remains.
How to withdraw permission for optional sample use, and what can still be done with results or samples already used, is stated.
Genetic analysis: who can see results, how they may be used, whether important findings may be returned, and the option not to receive such information.
items.applies_when: samples.genetic_analysis_optional or genetic analysis in the protocol

items.check: Research outside the approved protocol will not begin without prior Central Ethics Committee review.
Re-consent is planned when a participant who donated samples as a minor becomes an adult and gains full legal capacity.
The participant-related document is in Croatian (the cover letter too).
The Croatian text is professionally translated and proofread, not a literal global-template translation.
Croatia-specific authorities, costs, insurance, contacts, privacy rights and legal wording replace country-neutral text; no 'in your country' or 'in some countries'.
The title and text use the Croatian term Informirani pristanak consistently.
The main consent is one unified document, with all information before the signature section.
The first page identifies the trial and sponsor; headers and footers are in Croatian.
The planned number of participants globally and in Croatia is stated.
The sponsor bears all protocol-related costs, including treatment of trial-related injury.
Reimbursement is described accurately, with the maximum net amount in euros where applicable, consistent with P1.

Contraception and pregnancy follow-up wording matches the Croatian national specifics (both partners use reliable contraception where reproductive effects are unknown or potentially harmful) and the protocol risk.
Participant-rights questions are directed first to the investigator and the trial lead, with the Central Ethics Committee address for written rights questions after those routes.
Each document has a unique descriptive name, version and date matching CTIS.
Population, site, country, language and age band are clear in the file name and document header where useful.
Only the current version is in the submission package.
Signature labels identify the participant, legal representative, parent or guardian, physician or dentist interviewer and impartial witness correctly.
Date and time fields are included where the protocol or emergency process requires exact sequence evidence.
items.applies_when: consent.emergency_enrolment or protocol requires exact sequence evidence

items.check: The investigator delegation log will authorise the physician or dentist who conducts consent.
Recruitment materials, scripts, diaries, cards, questionnaires and instructions are versioned and dated.
No tracked changes, comments, placeholders, foreign contacts or inconsistent page numbers.
No drafting instruction remains in the final version ([bracket] notes, italic notes, '...........' gaps, yellow form labels).
Medical and regulatory terms are explained in plain Croatian.
Sentences and paragraphs are short enough for the intended population.
Risks are grouped and prioritised without hiding serious or likely effects in dense text.
Font, contrast, spacing, headings, tables and page breaks support reading and printing.
Signature pages remain visibly connected to the information and include the document identity.
Ages 4 to 7: assent uses simple illustrations, simple explanations and font no smaller than 20.
Ages 8 to 11: assent uses simple illustrations, simple explanations and font no smaller than 16.
Ages 12 to 14 and 15 to 17 have separate versions in an ordinary format with simpler language.
Croatian diacritics, capitalization, grammar and formal address (Vi, capitalised) are consistent.

After the content QC, the Croatia Part II document checklist (checklists/part-ii-package.json) is run: recruitment procedure, participant documents, investigator evidence, site evidence, insurance, financial arrangements, GDPR statement and biological-sample statement present when applicable.
